complexity.notes: Correctness is fragile: the scheme fails if any input string contains the magic delimiter 'paysutdlfmywvaugplk49w87ky9v478'; a length-prefixed encoding (e.g. 'len#string') is the standard robust approach. Also, decode('') on an empty encode returns [''] after pop, which is mishandled only by luck of the split/pop combination — edge cases with empty lists and empty strings should be verified. Using str.join/split is otherwise idiomatic.
complexity.summary: Encodes by joining the strings with a hardcoded 'unlikely' delimiter (plus a trailing delimiter), and decodes by splitting on that delimiter and dropping the empty trailing piece. Both operations are linear scans over the total character volume, which is O(n) since string lengths are bounded.
